title: The band bus and rapport with Armstrong
summary: Armstrong rode the band bus; Moore tells how he finally told him about hearing him at the Sunset in 1929.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: You used to travel around the country, you said, to the south and to California, he had his own band bus. He rode in the bus or did he ride in an automobile?

No, no, he always rode in tne bus. I have a lot of memories of him riding in the bus and the jokes they were telling each other and the dozens they play with each other, whenever we'd get through our performance anywhere, we can tell, all
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

of us, musicians can tell if Louie was in a happy mood or if he's tired and doesn't want to be bothered -- we left him alone and I've always had good rapport with Louie because I never asked him questions, anything personal or anything like that, I'd say, 'Hello, Pops, how do you feel? How's everything?' That's about all the relationship I had with Louie for a while. He came to the point where he felt like talking. He would come to my seat in the bus and we'd just rap, you know, about different subjects and music and how I happened to come to join his band. I told him about the time that I heard him back in the Sunset Cafe in 1929. Louie said, 'Gee, that's a nice story. Some day maybe you'll write your own memoirs or something.' Anyway, he was pleased to know I always wanted to play with him and that's the way he is, we talked about that on the bus.
